project_tracker_diagnostic: Perennial/subshrub with winged petiole bases that often fuse into conspicuous nodal discs; yellow-orange heads usually solitary or in 2s–3s; rough foliage.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common, conspicuous, or high-value comparison species for Central Texas field ID.

morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; petiole bases dilated/winged and often fused across the node into a disc; blades ovate, sometimes 3-lobed.
morphology_keys.heads: Usually solitary, sometimes 2–3; rays light orange-yellow, often brown/purple-lined beneath.
morphology_keys.fruit: Cypselae often with pappus absent or minute.
best_field_traits: At an intact opposite-leaf node, look for widened/winged petiole bases connecting across the stem into a nodal disc; this is the strongest practical recognition feature.
Perennial/subshrub with coarse hairy stems and ovate, sometimes three-lobed, opposite leaves.
Heads commonly single or in twos or threes; rays light orange-yellow, often dark-lined on undersides.
Compare Simsia lagasceiformis: usually annual, with different nodal-disc and root habit; do not rely on pappus absence alone, as it overlaps.
Crew photo sequence: whole plant; front/side node macro; underside of head; mature fruit with scale. Mark only visible structures on correctly identified licensed images.

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Prefer curated taxon photos plus multiple views from one Central Texas/Texas observation.
photo_strategy.remaining_need: PRIORITY 1: an actual close-up of opposite petiole bases expanded/fused into nodal discs (front and side, intact stem), followed by head underside and mature cypselae. No existing gallery image is confirmed to show the nodal disc clearly; do not place arrows on leaves or generic nodes. PRIORITY 2: use the already installed licensed head-underside view only if independently confirmed to be correct species and the precise phyllaries are visible. Annotation pending until actual pixels are inspected.
